correctness.rationale: For every unit vector, its uniquely normalized dual pairing is (a r^p+d+b r^(p-1)e^{iφ})/(1+r^p). Zero is attainable exactly when a continuous coercive scalar magnitude equals |b|. Minimizing its square after s=(D/A)z reduces to a quadratic with exactly one positive root z_p(c), including c=-1 zero and b=0. Applying the same formula to T^-1 yields reversed diagonal thresholds and the phase-independent exponent ratio. Strict monotonicity in phase follows via an exact envelope derivative. A normalized exact p=4 witness and analytic geometric-mean counterexamples verify the iff p=2 dichotomy. Independent standard-library numeric checks yielded 1111 finite diagnostics, not used to claim infinite proof.

value.rationale: Bračič–Diogo formulated simultaneous zero inclusion in finite-dimensional Banach geometry; the 2026 motivating implication is dimension-restricted. This result completely classifies, for every smooth complex ℓp² plane, whether every invertible operator must obey zero-inclusion symmetry, and gives the exact complex-angle off-diagonal phase intervals for all invertible triangular matrices. The angle-independent inversion ratio and continuously vanishing antipodal thresholds identify structural behavior beyond the already known positive-real-dissipativity slice. The finite-dimensional complete classification and explicit witnesses are independently useful for testing numerical-range and Birkhoff–James symmetry phenomena; no downstream paper-sized theorem is asserted.
